original_value: AbstractThe consensus‐reaching process (CRP) to achieve higher unanimity and ensure common agreement before deriving a final decision has become an important procedure in group decision‐making problems. The demand for high‐quality decision results has motivated the development of large‐scale group decision‐making (LGDM). In such cases, the issue of minority opinion has gained awareness due to the related effects on enhancing consensus and decision quality. A minority opinion cannot exert an effect unless the majority attach importance to whether that opinion is supported or not. To reflect the effect of minority opinions on consensus, this paper establishes a LGDM framework with an objective and interactive‐information‐based feedback mechanism for the CRP. Given the natural forms of human expression, multi‐granular linguistic information and a 2‐tuple linguistic model are used. First, initial weights are objectively assigned to decision‐makers (DMs) to weaken the impact of the majority. Subsequently, a non‐support degree function is newly defined to reflect the extent to which other DMs dissent from a minority opinion. More importantly, feedback rules are constructed to make corresponding adjustments to the powers of discourse among all DMs in the attempt to reach consensus. Finally, the proposed three‐phase LGDM framework is applied to new product development (NPD), and simulation experiments are conducted based on two algorithms to verify the framework's applicability and feasibility.

result.paraphrase: Abstract The consensus-reaching process (CRP), used to achieve greater unanimity and establish common agreement before a final decision is made, has become an important procedure in group decision-making problems. The need for high-quality decision outcomes has driven the development of large-scale group decision-making (LGDM). In such settings, minority opinion has attracted attention because of its effects on improving consensus and decision quality. A minority opinion can have no effect unless the majority cares whether it is supported or not. To capture the influence of minority opinions on consensus, this paper proposes an LGDM framework with an objective, interactive-information-based feedback mechanism for the CRP. In view of the natural forms of human expression, multi-granular linguistic information and a 2-tuple linguistic model are employed. First, initial weights are objectively assigned to decision-makers (DMs) to reduce the influence of the majority. Then, a non-support degree function is newly defined to show the extent to which other DMs disagree with a minority opinion. More importantly, feedback rules are constructed to adjust the discourse power of all DMs accordingly in an effort to reach consensus. Finally, the proposed three-phase LGDM framework is applied to new product development (NPD), and simulation experiments based on two algorithms are carried out to verify the framework's applicability and feasibility.
